## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical testing for real-time, GPU-accelerated inference with batching and multi-cluster deployments, focusing on latency guarantees, resilience, and privacy.

## Key Concepts

- End-to-end testing of streaming/batched inference workloads
- Latency budgets with p95/p99 guarantees across tenants
- Fault injection across GPU nodes, network partitions, and orchestration failures
- Multi-cluster canary and feature-flag testing in CI/CD pipelines
- Observability: metrics, distributed tracing, dashboards, and structured logging

## Code Example

```python
import pytest
from locust import HttpUser, task, between

class InferenceUser(HttpUser):
    wait_time = between(0.1, 0.5)
    
    @task
    def predict(self):
        payload = generate_sample()
        with self.client.post("/predict", json=payload, catch_response=True) as resp:
            if resp.elapsed.total_seconds() > 0.05:
                resp.failure("p95 latency exceeded")
            else:
                resp.success()
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests for client-side caching are practical and often overlooked. This question probes understanding of per-tab in-memory caches with TTL, fallback to localStorage, cross-tab consistency, offline resilience, and privacy constraints. It also touches real-world CI/test strategies for headless browsers and flaky networks.

## Key Concepts
- Client-side caching with TTL and eviction
- LocalStorage privacy and data classification
- Cross-tab coherence via BroadcastChannel
- Offline support and storage fallback
- Testing strategies: unit, integration, and end-to-end in CI with headless browsers

## Code Example
```javascript
// Example: simple TTL cache skeleton used for tests
class Cache { constructor() { this.store = new Map(); } set(key, value, ttlMs) { const expiry = Date.now() + ttlMs; this.store.set(key, { value, expiry }); } get(key) { const entry = this.store.get(key); if (!entry) return null; if (Date.now() > entry.expiry) { this.store.delete(key); return null; } return entry.value; } }
```
